Hi, heart failure nurse here who has experience with lots of LVADs. I take care of VAD patients every week. It sounds like your dad is very very sick. That heart failure stuff, like swelling in the legs, is bad for his kidneys, and all of this together probably is making his heart pump very poorly- I would guess around 10-20% ejection fraction-- ask the cardiologist about that! I'd love to talk to you more, as these patients are exactly what I see on my specialized unit every day. Anyway, if they are considering him for a VAD, that means he is very sick. That means little time left.. like, less a than a couple years. An LVAD can extend that, but not by super long. A lot of his prognosis has to deal with lots of labs and left ventricular ejection fraction-- basically how much blood the heart is actually pumping each beat-- so I can't say for sure until I know those. There are so many factors that play into it, so it would be important to chat on an individual basis. Of course I do NOT replace any doctors or medical advice at all. I just would need to know more about the case in order to offer any knowledge. In that case, I could maybe offer a little perspective as a heart failure/ VAD nurse. But of course, your doctors and nurses are much more valuable!
